THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. summary: Abstract. Spin-independent mα⁶ operators of lithium require singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals. We classify all supports of eight selected operator representations, obtaining 21 negative patterns, 12 finite-part families and 58 finite-part minimal rows. Every such row has four rational seed coordinates and an explicit polylogarithmic remainder. Generic non-isogeny and product monodromy make these coordinates unique; exactly 5 minimal rows are elliptic. Every reached pattern has a published treatment or a finite representation, with at most two residual variables where needed. A closed-form atlas of 98 functions includes 291 wall formulas and 174 ray formulas. The evaluator covers positive exact rational exponents; 1044 values at 18 points agree with independent evaluations of the formulas to 40 significant digits. At 9 further pre-specified points, all 522 values agree with an independent implementation of the same closed forms in every printed digit. Independent native quadratures confirm sampled values to 55 digits or more at 5 points spanning all four chambers. We compare 231 published reference values and classify the differences. A worked Q₄₄ matrix element proves that total basis degree three is the lowest admitting an element outside the algebraic-letter polylogarithmic class. Open questions include unresolved cone classifications, a smaller lower-function space on triangle walls, a complete seed form for the worked element, and missing native values. This record holds the manuscript (version 7; 53 pages), the verification bundle LITHIUM_QED_MASTER_P3_v7.zip (LaTeX source and PDF, the supplementary verification package with the census atlas, the wall and ray formulas, the selected representations, value tables, published-value comparisons, the unchanged closed-form evaluator and the replay script run_checks.py , the fact sheet and claim map that tie every statement to its source, and the provenance of the manuscript; 505 files, checked by MANIFEST.sha256 ), the clean arXiv LaTeX source, and SHA256SUMS.txt . README.md explains how to verify the files and run the checks; PAPER3_VERIFICATION/README.md inside the bundle is the entry point for the replay. Matuzas, Three-electron Hylleraas integrals with two inverse-square distances: exact reduction and high-precision evaluation for the fine structure of lithium, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23977551 . A useful 4D aroma civilization must know when not to release any molecule. It must measure the real power consumed by ventilation, protect accessible withdrawal of consent, resist stale sensors, document reference material identities and preserve digital-twin state and uncertainty for future reconstruction. Complete CSV equality alone cannot prove any environmental benefit. Future investigators may replace a sophisticated controller with a cheaper conventional system and publish the negative result. This research volume separates 4D material sorption from passive airflow, audited microgrid energy from shifted HVAC costs, fairness and accessible refusal from personalized preference scores, preserved digital twins from physically correct sensor calibration, and software stop requests from electrically witnessed hardware isolation. F191 through F195 share an indoor-air model boundary but retain independent endpoints, conventional benchmarks and authority stops. All surfaces and scenarios are synthetic and cannot establish real building safety, human exposure or clinical benefit. F191 / 4D Smart Aroma Materials in Living Environments at the Limit. Mechanism: reversible sorption, material transport, surface state and geometry-memory response, temperature-dependent desorption, ventilation advection-diffusion and material state history. Independent endpoint 4D surface response reproducibility [%]. Minimum prototype: synthetic shape-memory polymer-state trajectories, sealed nonrelease sorption grids, programmable humidity traces, certified test artefacts and mechanical-interlock witness logs. Strong conventional comparator matched nonresponsive passive adsorbent plus ventilation-only and fixed-rate no-release offline baselines. Witness: unaffiliated materials laboratory with gravimetric sorption, blind dimensional cycles and independently calibrated room-concentration reference. Counterworld: withheld humidity reversal and changed ventilation topology after frozen response calibration. Stop: nonconsensual release, material leak, unverified concentration, uncontrolled heating or measured air-quality exceedance. Mechanism: power-flow scheduling, energy integration, battery state-of-charge, heat and ventilation energy, volatile-source mass balance and demand-response constraints. Independent endpoint Aroma control energy cost [kWh/day]. Minimum prototype: offline 24-hour synthetic building demand traces, traceable unit conversion sheets, no-release actuator emulation, battery state files and blinded grid-fault challenge packets. Strong conventional comparator measured-energy conventional HVAC and fixed-release/no-release scheduling with equal air-quality and grid constraints. Witness: independent energy auditor using traceable revenue-grade power meters, ventilation references and battery SoC logging. Counterworld: blind renewable shortfall combined with a late-night ventilation demand spike. Stop: ventilation below regulatory minimum, unsafe exposure forecast, battery reserve failure, energy-meter trace loss or violation of human stop authority. Mechanism: protected-subgroup gap estimands, occupancy-independent air quality, consent and opt-out states, accessibility constraints, spatial exposure heterogeneity and multiobjective constrained control. A useful 4D aroma civilization must know when not to release any molecule. It must measure the real power consumed by ventilation, protect accessible withdrawal of consent, resist stale sensors, document reference material identities and preserve digital-twin state and uncertainty for future reconstruction. Complete CSV equality alone cannot prove any environmental benefit. Future investigators may replace a sophisticated controller with a cheaper conventional system and publish the negative result. summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 39 / F191–F195 4D AROMA ENVIRONMENTS AND AUTONOMOUS LIVING CIVILIZATION FIVE FLAGSHIP SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ESSENCE / PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL / 2026-11-23 SCIENTIFIC DNA AND BOUNDARIES. This research volume separates 4D material sorption from passive airflow, audited microgrid energy from shifted HVAC costs, fairness and accessible refusal from personalized preference scores, preserved digital twins from physically correct sensor calibration, and software stop requests from electrically witnessed hardware isolation. F191 through F195 share an indoor-air model boundary but retain independent endpoints, conventional benchmarks and authority stops. All surfaces and scenarios are synthetic and cannot establish real building safety, human exposure or clinical benefit. F191 / 4D Smart Aroma Materials in Living Environments at the Limit. Mechanism: reversible sorption, material transport, surface state and geometry-memory response, temperature-dependent desorption, ventilation advection-diffusion and material state history. Independent endpoint 4D surface response reproducibility [%]. Minimum prototype: synthetic shape-memory polymer-state trajectories, sealed nonrelease sorption grids, programmable humidity traces, certified test artefacts and mechanical-interlock witness logs. A useful 4D aroma civilization must know when not to release any molecule. It must measure the real power consumed by ventilation, protect accessible withdrawal of consent, resist stale sensors, document reference material identities and preserve digital-twin state and uncertainty for future reconstruction. Complete CSV equality alone cannot prove any environmental benefit. Future investigators may replace a sophisticated controller with a cheaper conventional system and publish the negative result. A useful 4D aroma civilization must know when not to release any molecule. It must measure the real power consumed by ventilation, protect accessible withdrawal of consent, resist stale sensors, document reference material identities and preserve digital-twin state and uncertainty for future reconstruction. Complete CSV equality alone cannot prove any environmental benefit. Future investigators may replace a sophisticated controller with a cheaper conventional system and publish the negative result. summary: In multireference alignment one observes noisy copies of a signal in R^d, each cyclically shifted by an unknown random amount. The quasi maximum likelihood estimator aligns the observations jointly and averages them. Its power spectrum is biased, and Bandeira asked whether its Fourier phases are consistent once the power spectrum is corrected. They are not. Take d equal to 6, 7, 10 or 11 and the truth a unit sinusoid of frequency one. At every sufficiently large fixed noise level, the phase of the first Fourier coefficient of the estimate converges to the set of midpoints between consecutive shifts of the true phase. If the Fourier magnitudes of the estimate are then replaced by the true ones, its distance to the nearest shift of the truth converges to 2 sin(π/(2d)). The same failure holds on an open set of signals whose nonconstant Fourier coefficients are all nonzero. The deciding sign is that of an explicit Gaussian integral, which we enclose in rigorous bounds for every d from 3 to 11.
title: A half-step phase error of the hard-alignment estimator in multireference alignment

summary: Synthetic operational databases from process-based business simulation are commonly judged by resemblance to real data, which misses plausible records that could not have arisen from the process they represent. We define business-rule admissibility as the property that every state and every change in a dataset could have been produced by the represented process under its own rules, decompose it into ten criteria, each checkable as a query over a database and its change history, and name three layers where a simulation can lose it. We draw 22 cases from developing NAILU, a framework that turns business prose into executable simulations. Separate language-model agents built a study firm from its handbook; another, seeing neither the model nor its data, wrote the firm’s rules. Of nine past defects re-injected, the rules caught six in every run; seven event-log distances caught two in every run, one of them missed by the rules, and a third in most runs; the firm’s management indicators caught one only when read monthly with measures the author added, and none under a robust score. A pre-registered replication on twenty new seeds confirmed all five predictions. Of five further defects, covering a forbidden transition, recording and execution, the rules caught three in every run and one in half; one that dropped writes from the change history escaped every detector but its reconciliation with the tables. On the unchanged firm, the rules found six departures from its handbook. The evidence comes from one framework, where the detectors saw different defects
title: Business-Rule Admissibility in Process-Based Business Simulation

summary: This a research program titled the "Triple Interface Method". Its aim is to solve the Goldbach conjecture.  This manuscript presents a modular tripartite “engine” for tackling the binary Goldbach problem. The argument is broken into a small set of auditable modules—how energy is spread across rational frequencies, how bilinear short-shift correlations are controlled, how nuisance low-frequency effects are cancelled, and how average positivity is converted into pointwise positivity for every even number in a range. Each outputs a quantitative bound; together they feed a simple closing ledger that leaves only mild, standard number-theory inputs (distribution in very small moduli and a positive main term) and a routine finite base. The machinery of the paper has been coded in Lean 4 and the repo is available to the public. This proof strategy was not successful. It is preserved here for the purposes of the archive.
title: Goldbach and the Triple Interface Method

summary: Spatial pixel binning of a dataset and tidier menus. The format stays enginir-1.7 ; projects without binned datasets are unchanged. Added Spatial pixel binning of a dataset. Add Dataset's Binning (2 × 2, 3 × 3, 4 × 4) and Project.add_dataset(path, binning=k) average k × k blocks of frames and rows every time the file is read, before the reference correction. Counts stay counts (the mean is rounded and keeps the file's integer type), so levels, references, ROIs and models work unchanged on the binned pixels. Reference frames are frames of the file as stored. A file has one binning in a project, fixed when it is added. A model records its binning: a new scan is binned like the model to be predicted, a scan registered with another binning is refused, and a calibration set mixing binnings is refused. enginir.io.bin_blocks , bin_rows and bin_frame_chunks do the same on arrays. The format stays enginir-1.7 ; the binning is stored only for binned datasets. engiNIR 1.7.4 opens a project with a binned dataset and refits its models from the stored ROIs, but refuses its data file (the shape differs) rather than read it unbinned. Removed The Band image panel (View > Band image): it showed no more than the Spatial image.

summary: Data, fitted models, forecasts and reproducibility code accompanying “Consistency Distillation with Soft Feasibility Penalties and Copula Coupling for Joint Wind-Solar-Load Probabilistic Forecasting”. The archive contains Belgian wind, solar and load hindcasts at 1 h and 24 h, strong tree baselines, retained neural weights and ensembles, calibration and joint-dependence diagnostics, figure source data and table-generation code. Separate experiments examine archived-weather wind forecasts under matched training budgets and complete inference costs for fixed core policies. The weather-budget experiment and inference-cost benchmark use different models and must not be combined into one accuracy–latency claim. The eight ZIP files together form a self-contained archive. Download all parts and extract them into the same directory; each is an ordinary ZIP, not a split volume. ARCHIVE_PARTS.md lists the required files. README.md and REPRODUCE.md describe the directory structure and reproduction commands; MANIFEST.json provides per-file SHA-256 values. Results include negative findings and do not establish qualified-teacher accuracy retention or operational superiority. Author-owned code: MIT. Original experimental results: CC BY 4.0. Open-Meteo snapshots use best_match; per-value upstream model identities were not retained. The provider API-data licence and this provenance limitation are documented separately.
title: Data and code for Consistency Distillation with Soft Feasibility Penalties and Copula Coupling for Joint Wind-Solar-Load Probabilistic Forecasting

summary: We establish a deterministic algorithm that computes the exact closed meandric number M_n from the order n in 2^{O(sqrt(n) log n)} bit operations. The main construction splits each crossing into two points and gives a bijection between closed plane meanders and a prescribed class of straight-line Hamilton cycles on a rational point set of size 4n. A polynomial-size system of local annotations selects exactly one constrained Delaunay triangulation for each cycle. Applying the annotated-triangulation counting theorem of Marx and Miltzow then yields the subexponential bound. We make the geometric construction, the uniqueness of every annotation and the integer-arithmetic cost explicit. A technical appendix gives a periodic-depth realization with canonical rooted-path states and the same asymptotic bound. As a separate consequence, an interval decomposition and formal Lagrange inversion give an exact coefficient formula and a subexponential algorithm for an associated core count; these cores are exponentially rare among all meanders. Reproducible finite checks are reported separately from the proof and from larger reference counts. Version 2.0 (22 November 2026): revised and simplified proof of the main reduction, with an explicit c*N^15 bound for the essential annotation catalogue; clearer attribution to the general Marx--Miltzow counting framework; the depth-augmented realization moved to a technical appendix; removal of the former core-coverage theorem section; expanded bibliography and precise reference-count provenance; and reproducible positive, negative and rank-feasibility diagnostics. The accompanying source archive contains editable LaTeX, BibTeX, vector figures, standard-library Python checks and raw records. It does not implement or benchmark the full subexponential counting engine at large orders. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.
title: Exact Subexponential Counting of Closed Plane Meanders

summary: Abstract Introduction: The polymeric product obtained in the presence of microheterogeneous catalytic systems is characterized by a fairly reasonable molecular weight distribution (MWD), resulting from kinetically non-equivalent active centers (ACs) in the system that initiates the polymerization process. The nature and composition of the ACs are determined by defining and solving an inverse problem in MWD formation. This problem is acute because revealing the nature of the kinetic heterogeneity explains the changes in molecular parameters and product consumption for different catalyst compositions and propagation modes in polymerizations. Objective: This study aimed to develop methods and algorithms for interpreting gel chromatograms to analyze the kinetic heterogeneity of an industrially obtained polymeric product in microheterogeneous catalytic systems. Methods: The solution method assumes that the MWD formed is a superposition of distributions inherent to each type of AC. Since the problem in the final formulation refers to Fredholm integral equations of the first type, the regularization method of A. N. Tikhonov is used for its numerical solution, with the original problem being preliminarily discretized. This methodology and the developed software algorithms were used to determine the kinetic heterogeneity of catalytic systems containing titanium and neodymium. Results and discussion: MWD analysis revealed two types of CAs with an average molecular weight of A̅T1 - lnM = 11.3 and B̅T1 - lnM = 13.2 in the titanium catalyst, and three types of A̅Nd - lnM = 11.1, B̅Nd - lnM = 12.7 and C̅Nd - lnM = 14 for the neodymium catalyst, respectively. Conclusions: Repeated computational experiments under different polymerization conditions and requirements for the preparation of a catalytic system allow us to reveal a relationship with the resulting heterogeneity of CAs. It allows us to define and solve problems related to controlling the molecular characteristics of the resulting polymer product. Resumo Introdução: o produto polimérico obtido na presença de sistemas catalíticos microheterogêneos é caracterizado por uma distribuição de peso molecular bastante razoável (MWD), resultante de centros ativos cineticamente não equivalentes (ACs) no sistema que inicia o processo de polimerização. A natureza e a composição dos ACs são determinadas definindo e resolvendo um problema inverso na formação de MWD. Este problema é agudo porque revelar a natureza da heterogeneidade cinética explica as mudanças nos parâmetros moleculares e de consumo do produto para diferentes composições de catalisador e modos de propagação em polimerizações. Objetivo: o presente estudo teve como objetivo desenvolver métodos e algoritmos de interpretação de cromatogramas em gel para analisar a heterogeneidade cinética de um produto polimérico obtido industrialmente em sistemas catalíticos microheterogêneos. Métodos: o método de solução parte do pressuposto de que o MWD formado é uma superposição de distribuições inerentes a cada tipo de ACs. Como o problema na formulação final se refere às equações integrais de Fredholm do primeiro tipo, o método de regularização de A. N. Tikhonov é usado para sua solução numérica, com o problema original sendo preliminarmente discretizado. Esta metodologia e os algoritmos de software desenvolvidos foram usados para determinar a heterogeneidade cinética de sistemas catalíticos contendo titânio e neodímio. Resultados e discussão: a análise MWD revelou dois tipos de ACs com um peso molecular médio de A̅T1 - lnM = 11.3 e B̅T1 - lnM = 13.2 no catalisador de titânio, e três tipos de A̅Nd - lnM = 11.1, B̅Nd - lnM = 12.7 e C̅Nd - lnM = 14 para o catalisador de neodímio, respectivamente. Conclusões: experimentos computacionais repetidos sob diferentes condições de polimerização e requisitos para a preparação de um sistema catalítico permitem revelar uma relação com a heterogeneidade resultante de ACs. summary: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models Text-to-image models are often assumed to be reproducible when the prompt and the random seed are fixed. The paper shows that this does not hold on GPUs. The same prompt and seed can produce a different image when the request is processed inside a batch instead of alone (batch size 1), and the result also changes across GPU models. Replaying exactly the same call is bit-exact, so the differences come from the execution setting (batch shape, numerical precision, GPU) and not from random sampling. This record provides every image used in the image-level analysis of the paper: 3,536 PNG images from 5 models (Qwen-Image-2.1, FLUX 3 Klein, HiDream-O1, Emu3.5 and Janus-Pro-7B), organized into 10 runs. For each prompt: solo images (batch 1, generated twice), batched images and verbatim replays. A static web viewer that shows these images side by side. For each image it tells you whether it is bit-identical to the batch-1 reference and, if not, gives its pixel MAE. Contents t2i_viewer.zip (~73 MB): the viewer, with a small sample (prompts 0, 4 and 8 of every run, 224 images). dataset_test.zip (~1 GB): the full dataset: all 3,536 images, run metadata ( run.json per run), the viewer data file ( manifest.js ) and the original provenance records ( _source/ ). How to view the images No installation is needed, only a web browser. Unzip t2i_viewer.zip and open t2i_viewer/index.html . It shows the sample. To see all the images, unzip dataset_test.zip , copy the resulting dataset_test folder inside t2i_viewer/ (replacing the sample) and reload index.html . The viewer lets you choose a run (model + GPU), a cross-GPU comparison (Janus-Pro-7B on RTX 6000 Ada vs RTX A6000) and, for Janus-Pro-7B, the decoding mode. The amplified difference map in the comparison view needs the folder to be served over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 8000 inside t2i_viewer/ ). Runs Ten runs, all in bf16: Qwen-Image-2.1 (RTX 6000 Ada, 10 and 100 prompts), FLUX 3 Klein (RTX 6000 Ada, 10 and 100 prompts), HiDream-O1 (RTX 6000 Ada, 100 prompts), Emu3.5 (H100 NVL, 10 prompts) and Janus-Pro-7B (RTX 6000 Ada and RTX A6000, 10 and 100 prompts each). Prompt ids are shared across models. File names (arms) A0.png : solo generation, batch size 1 (the reference). A1.png : solo rerun with the same configuration (bit-identical to A0 in all runs). B_<tag>.png : the same prompt and seed generated inside a batch (e.g. b16-r00-s11 = batch size 16, round 0, slot 11). R_<tag>.png , C_<tag>.png : verbatim replay of a batched call (bit-identical to its batched image in all runs). Janus-Pro-7B file names have a decoding-mode prefix ( sampled- or greedy- ), each with its own A0 reference. Metrics Computed on decoded RGB pixels. Exact means bit-identical RGB data. MAE is the mean absolute pixel difference (0–255 scale) against the A0 of the same prompt and decoding mode. The values are stored in manifest.js and reproduce the paper. Provenance The images were collected from the experiment servers into two dumps ( T2I_v12_images_full_janus_20261121 and T2I_v12_images_full_nonjanus_20261121_b ) and renamed into this layout without modifying their content. The original manifests (with SHA-256 for every image; all 3,536 images match), the collection journal and contact sheets are kept in dataset_test/_source/ . The SDXL images and the fp8/int8 variants discussed in the paper are not included. The images were generated with third-party models; the terms of use of each model may also apply to its outputs.
title: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models: Images and Viewer

summary: NovaFabric is self-hosted, open-source replay and evidence infrastructure for AI agents and agentic systems. It captures agent executions as portable, secret-scanned Run Capsules and provides replay, behavioral and structural diff, lineage, cryptographic provenance, assurance, and audit around those executions. The same capture layer can wrap general commands and runs entirely in the user's own infrastructure, from local environments through Kubernetes to SLURM/HPC, with no accounts and no telemetry. It is built around five primitives — Asset Registry, Run Capsule, Replay, Lineage, and Evidence Bundle — and five explicit replay modes (forensic, mocked, semantic, exact, and the experimental intervention mode). Run Capsules can be sealed with the user’s own key; sealing is opt-in. Evidence bundles verify offline using only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier, with no NovaFabric installation required. Interoperates with established specifications rather than inventing formats: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 timestamping, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, and CycloneDX.
title: NovaFabric: replayable, verifiable execution evidence for AI agents

summary: A pre-registrable experimental protocol for testing whether the apparent "self" of an LLM agent behaves as a localised, persistent substrate ( ātman ), as a process assembled from the five aggregates with no fixed substrate ( anattā ), or as a surface regularity with no internal organisation (null). It specifies four studies: (1) localisation probes, with targeted, mean and random feature ablation and capability controls; (2) framing invariance of self-descriptions across system personas, languages, registers and role-play framings; (3) aggregate-wise decomposition of activations (rūpa, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhāra, viññāṇa); and (4) impermanence and re-composition across sessions with external memory. It treats self-reports as evidence only when activation-level probes agree with them, and controls for instruction-following, e.g. a model that says "I have no self" after a Buddhist prompt. Provenance. The author wrote this protocol by June 2026 and kept it private in his Notion workspace, attached to the lab page "2026-06-10 – Wadduwage lab summer work plan" under the "citta transformer" project. The file deposited here is byte-for-byte that Notion attachment. summary: Software overview SMART-TDAH is an educational web platform for visualising and analysing students’ exercise results and progress. It combines a React frontend, a Node.js/Express backend and a PostgreSQL connection. It provides user management, progress charts and tables, four interface languages (Galician, Spanish, English and Brazilian Portuguese), and optional language-model-assisted queries through Gemini, LLaMA and Mixtral integrations. Package contents This deposit archives commit 388620adbd23d7793e3af7fec98c6e46a3fea5eb of the Chair’s repository. The package contains 58 original source and resource files, including frontend, backend, dependency manifests and lockfiles, README and GNU GPLv3 licence. A provenance note and file manifest are added. No student database, database dump, API keys or environment credential file is included. Requirements and usage The README documents Node.js 18 or later, npm 9 or later and PostgreSQL 14 or later. Install dependencies separately in the backend and frontend directories. Configure PostgreSQL and API credentials through a local backend .env file. Start the backend with node server.js from its directory and the frontend with npm start . The backend package has no npm start script in this archived version. Database provisioning and credentials must be supplied by the deploying institution. Dependencies and external API services retain their respective terms. The project involved educational collaboration with Floriano and Barão de Grajaú, Brazil. Institutional thesis record . The deposit describes a technical and educational result; it does not establish diagnostic validity, clinical certification or independently quantified adoption. summary: (PT) Este artigo, primeiro de uma trilogia dedicada ao prolongamento do Itinerário Complementar 6 (IC6) e ao futuro da Região Metropolitana de Coimbra (RMC), discute a relação entre a melhoria das acessibilidades e a construção de um projeto de desenvolvimento territorial à escala regional. Partindo da urgência de concluir a ligação rodoviária no eixo Tábua–Oliveira do Hospital–Seia, o texto defende que a concretização da infraestrutura não deve depender da definição prévia de uma estratégia regional, mas que ambas as questões devem ser discutidas no presente. O IC6 permitirá reduzir obstáculos à mobilidade quotidiana, facilitar o acesso a serviços e diminuir custos para famílias e empresas, respondendo a necessidades de territórios onde já existem atividades, relações e oportunidades que importa reforçar. O artigo questiona, contudo, a ideia de que a melhoria das acessibilidades, por si só, assegura o desenvolvimento territorial ou contraria a perda de população. Defende que a consolidação da Região Metropolitana de Coimbra depende da capacidade de transformar a proximidade física em relações de trabalho, formação, cooperação e acesso a serviços, valorizando os diferentes centros urbanos e os lugares que estruturam a região. A reflexão propõe, assim, que a reivindicação do IC6 seja acompanhada por uma discussão mais ampla sobre a urbanidade que se pretende construir, entendendo a região metropolitana não apenas como um território de distâncias mais curtas, mas como um sistema de relações e oportunidades partilhadas. Publicado no Diário As Beiras , em 2 de novembro de 2026, p. 20, na rubrica urbanidadeS . (EN) This article, the first in a trilogy devoted to the extension of the IC6 road and the future of the Coimbra Metropolitan Region (RMC), examines the relationship between improved accessibility and the development of a territorial project at the regional scale. Starting from the urgent need to complete the road connection along the Tábua–Oliveira do Hospital–Seia corridor, the article argues that the construction of this infrastructure should not depend on the prior definition of a regional strategy, but that both issues must be addressed in the present. The IC6 will help reduce obstacles to everyday mobility, improve access to services and lower costs for households and businesses, responding to the needs of territories where activities, relationships and opportunities already exist. The article nevertheless challenges the assumption that improved accessibility alone can ensure territorial development or reverse population decline. It argues that consolidating the Coimbra Metropolitan Region depends on the ability to transform physical proximity into opportunities for employment, education, cooperation and access to services, while strengthening the different urban centres and settlements that structure the region. The discussion therefore proposes that the demand for the IC6 should be accompanied by a broader debate on the kind of urbanity to be developed, understanding the metropolitan region not merely as a territory of shorter distances, but as a system of interconnected places, relationships and shared opportunities. Originally published in Diário As Beiras , 2 November 2026, p. 20, in the urbanidadeS column.
title: IC6: um itinerário para consolidar uma região metropolitana?

Independent witness: second institution independently executing a fully versioned protocol with raw instrument traces, all attempts and signed stop records. Stop: unauthorized actuator command, unlogged anomaly, primary endpoint not independently verifiable or failed safe stop and audit trail. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 25 / F121-F125 QUANTUM CHEMISTRY OF BOTANICAL AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH WORKING EDITION V1.0 / PROSPECTIVE, NONCLINICAL, FALSIFIABLE, NUMERICALLY REPRODUCIBLE SCIENTIFIC IDENTITY AND NONCLAIM BOUNDARY Family 25 invites future molecular researchers to test five distinct hypotheses: electronic-structure reference accuracy, stereochemically resolved conformer ranking, conditional ligand and olfactory receptor interaction energies, oxidation transition-state errors, and wavelength-dependent photochemical degradation rates. Each question has a different kind of observable. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. FIVE INDIVIDUAL FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F121 / Quantum-Chemical Simulation of Aroma Electronic Structure at the Limit The proposed physical object is electronic-structure prediction of authenticated botanical odorant molecules, with emphasis on electron correlation, density functional approximation, basis-set incompleteness, spin state, reference geometry, stereochemistry, pseudopotential choice and convergence diagnostics. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. summary: Abstract. Spin-independent mα⁶ operators of lithium require singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals. We classify all supports of eight selected operator representations, obtaining 21 negative patterns, 12 finite-part families and 58 finite-part minimal rows. Every such row has four rational seed coordinates and an explicit polylogarithmic remainder. Generic non-isogeny and product monodromy make these coordinates unique; exactly 5 minimal rows are elliptic. Every reached pattern has a published treatment or a finite representation, with at most two residual variables where needed. A closed-form atlas of 98 functions includes 291 wall formulas and 174 ray formulas. The evaluator covers positive exact rational exponents; 1044 values at 18 points agree with independent evaluations of the formulas to 40 significant digits. At 9 further pre-specified points, all 522 values agree with an independent implementation of the same closed forms in every printed digit. Independent native quadratures confirm sampled values to 55 digits or more at 5 points spanning all four chambers. We compare 231 published reference values and classify the differences. A worked Q₄₄ matrix element proves that total basis degree three is the lowest admitting an element outside the algebraic-letter polylogarithmic class. Open questions include unresolved cone classifications, a smaller lower-function space on triangle walls, a complete seed form for the worked element, and missing native values. This record holds the manuscript (version 7; 53 pages), the verification bundle LITHIUM_QED_MASTER_P3_v7.zip (LaTeX source and PDF, the supplementary verification package with the census atlas, the wall and ray formulas, the selected representations, value tables, published-value comparisons, the unchanged closed-form evaluator and the replay script run_checks.py , the fact sheet and claim map that tie every statement to its source, and the provenance of the manuscript; 505 files, checked by MANIFEST.sha256 ), the clean arXiv LaTeX source, and SHA256SUMS.txt . README.md explains how to verify the files and run the checks; PAPER3_VERIFICATION/README.md inside the bundle is the entry point for the replay. The code is under the MIT licence; the manuscript and the data are under CC BY 4.0. Companion articles: J. Matuzas, Elliptic structure of the singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23917908 ; J. Matuzas, Three-electron Hylleraas integrals with two inverse-square distances: exact reduction and high-precision evaluation for the fine structure of lithium, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23977551 . Generative-AI disclosure and author responsibility. ChatGPT-6 Pro (GPT-6 Astra Pro in writing the manuscript) was used for derivations, computations, and drafting; OpenAI Codex ran the independent native computations and the independent evaluator tests on a local server; Claude Opus 5.5, with Claude Fable 5.2 in parts of the census review and of the evaluator tests, was used for independent re-derivation and audit of every increment and proposed several of the checks. The author directed and audited the work throughout and takes full responsibility for the mathematics and the final text. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 81V45; Secondary 33E05, 33B30, 14H52, 65D30, 81-08. All the work was done by AI. Preprint. External peer review is not claimed.

Reverse Metaanalysis

summary: GHC compares successful rewrite rules in arrival order. We ask when changing how rules are tried preserves the chosen rewrite. If every match of a later strict challenger implies a match of its earlier incumbent, a depth-first search gives a faithful first-match priority in linear time once the comparisons are known. Appending a challenger preserves old relative priorities. Inserting a structural rule before $t$ old arrivals can force almost all $\binom{t}{2}$ suffix pairs to reverse, even if the new rule never wins. An inherited list can need quadratically many reversals with only one later arrival. Given the caller table, minimum repair takes polynomial time for fixed $t$. For insertion at the head the decision problem is NP-complete even when every old rule can still win. The containment criterion covers sixteen shipped list-fold rules, including three with cyclic pairwise choices. For a fixed arrival order, testing whether the last rule can be deleted takes polynomial time on a forest of forward comparisons and is coNP-complete at treewidth two, even with disjoint one-to-one match prerequisites. Deciding whether one first-match priority preserves all winners takes polynomial time at width two and is coNP-complete at width three. For a list of $q$ possible winners, a width-two algorithm has an exponent linear in $q$, with a matching conditional lower bound. Typed Core templates realize the reductions at the GHC 9.14.1 matcher. A separate joint-order problem becomes NP-complete at three successes per call. The fold example compares the source-level work of shared tests.

summary: Abstract Biological semiosis is a relational hypothesis whose attribution depends on evidence, causal explanation and an explicit interpretive theory. Elementary Semiotic Events provides an episode-level procedure for evaluating this inference. Each claim specifies a candidate sign, object, interpreting system and interpretant, alongside the observations and warrants linking them. Four obligations govern assessment: define the theory-relative relation, establish its biological premises, test the inferential bridge independently and evaluate rivals. ESE distinguishes formal derivability, empirical support and permission to make a theoretical attribution. Its three-valued readiness policy records failed, unresolved or satisfied obligations; chronological traces preserve the availability of evidence; and a finite-model criterion tests identifiability. Constructed examples show how a selective response can leave reference unsettled and observationally equivalent mechanisms can disagree under intervention. Transcription factor–DNA (TF–DNA) recognition provides a tractable molecular specialization, connecting sequence models, binding, regulation and interpretant hypotheses through distinct measurements. These results establish conditional properties of explicit assessment procedures and identify possible discriminating biological tests. summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half (π), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ)², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial prin

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Fifty entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature, among them: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7; a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients; a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset; a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten; a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998); a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation; a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight; a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. Light through a Jerlov water type. The package: computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963); converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors; gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m, and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers; integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth; gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two; and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent; ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum; carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models; converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient. Measurements it carries. Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type, against which the depth profile is checked; Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille; the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures; Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters; five published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016), Lee et al. (2015) and Morel et al. (2007), for the caller to choose from; the eight stations of the clearest ocean water measured, Morel et al. (2007); the measured reflectance of ten materials found in and around water, from the USGS Spectral Library Version 7, for reference images of how they look through each water type. Without a water type. It gives: Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001, and the earlier edition of Morel 1988), or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013); the attenuation of the visible and of the whole shortwave from the surface to a depth, and the depth where a given fraction of the visible light is left, the euphotic depth among them, from the absorption and backscattering coefficients at 490 nm and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2007); from chlorophyll, the absorption by phytoplankton (Bricaud et al. 1995) and the b

The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been.
